doc.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: His mother's work and the family singing
summary: His mother cleaned offices for $2 a week and bought Hank a piano; the children sang spirituals and quartets at home, and Olivvia taught voice.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So can you talk about your mother? You’ve talked about your father, but can you talk about your mother? I imagine with that many kids she was a housewife.

My mother to me she was a saint. I guess she worked herself to death. She used to buy us shoes and clothes and things during the depression. She worked for an office building in downtown Pontiac. So it was dentists and doctors and people like that’d and we’d go down there and help her and she’d clean that whole building for $2 a week! So she had a lot of fortitude. With that $2 she bought Hank a piano—she knew how to use it!

Sounds like she was very encouraging about music in the household Nothing would make her happier than to see her kids practicing, singing together. We did a lot of that. We had quartets. We sang negro spirituals
So she would have you sing in the house/
Oh yeah sure in the house!

Except the only place we couldn’t sing was at the dinner table. I remember Thad was singing that song called “Steamboat Bill” [Elvin imitates the song and sings the melody] “Steamboat Bill! Du du du da da da! Steamboat Bill” (laughs) and my father said to Thad “Shut up before I hit you in the head with this spoon” – BONG! (Elvin laughs). He rang like a gong! Oh boy.
So was Hank the first one of your brothers and sisters to become involved musically
Oh no it was Olivvia she was the first, she was so talented that she used to give a girl who lived near us, her name was Pauline McCahon, Olivvia gave her voice lessons and
she eventually became a part of the Metropolitan Opera company and her stage name was Carlotta Franzel.
